title: Products and exponentials in the Joyal homotopy category
statement:
Use the Joyal model structure and categorical equivalences of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], the coherent-nerve adjunction $\mathfrak C\dashv N_{\mathrm{hc}}$ of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], in fixed nested universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$ with small meaning $\mathcal U$-small and categories fitting in $\mathcal U'$. Write $h\mathsf{sSet}_{\mathrm J}$ for the ordinary localization of simplicial sets at categorical equivalences, and $[X,Y]_{\mathrm J}$ for its Hom sets. For simplicial sets $K,L$, their degreewise product represents the categorical product in this homotopy category, and the natural functor
$$\mathfrak C[K\times L]\longrightarrow\mathfrak C[K]\times\mathfrak C[L]$$
is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. For every quasicategory $Q$, define $\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{sSet}}(K\times\Delta^n,Q)$. This is a quasicategory, and evaluation induces natural bijections
$$[X,\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)]_{\mathrm J}\ \cong\ [X\times K,Q]_{\mathrm J}.$$
These bijections use the actual simplicial evaluation map. In particular $\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)$ represents $[Q]^{[K]}$ in the Joyal homotopy category, not just an exponential of ordinary homotopy categories.

source.place: Corollaries 2.2.5.4 and 2.2.5.6, Proposition 2.2.5.7, and the proof of Proposition 1.2.7.3 printed pp.92-94; products of simplicial categories preserve DK equivalences as used there. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy-theoretic result.

proof.text: First verify that the stated internal Hom is a quasicategory. A horn $\Lambda_i^n\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)$ transposes to a map $K\times\Lambda_i^n\to Q$. Apply [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product] to the inner horn inclusion and $\varnothing\hookrightarrow K$: its pushout-product is $K\times\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow K\times\Delta^n$, up to interchanging factors, and is inner anodyne. Here an inner horn is inner anodyne because every inner fibration lifts against it by definition. Since $Q\to\Delta^0$ is an inner fibration, the transposed map extends, giving the required horn filler. All sets and maps remain in the chosen universe.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 1.2.7.3(1), printed p.94; Corollary 2.3.2.4.

proof.text: Products with any simplicial set preserve categorical equivalences. Indeed, for $u:A\to B$ a categorical equivalence, any $K$, and any test quasicategory $C$, simplicial currying gives isomorphisms $\operatorname{Fun}(B\times K,C)\cong\operatorname{Fun}(B,\operatorname{Fun}(K,C))$ and the corresponding isomorphism for $A$. Step 1 makes the new target $\operatorname{Fun}(K,C)$ a quasicategory. Use the current conventions of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure], which now refers directly to the enhanced-diagram conventions: its standard simplices, degreewise products and inner-horn definition of quasicategory agree with the ones in Step 1 and in the displayed currying formulas. By that node's testing definition, restriction along $u$ induces an equivalence after applying $h$ to the latter functor simplicial sets; hence restriction along $u\times1_K$ does too. This holds for every $C$, so $u\times1_K$ is a categorical equivalence. Factoring $u\times v$ as $(u\times1)$ followed by $(1\times v)$ proves the same for products of two categorical equivalences. The strict product bifunctor therefore descends to the ordinary localization: first localize in each variable, using this preservation of inverted arrows.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.5.4, printed p.92; direct argument from the categorical-equivalence testing convention already supplied by the DAG.

proof.text: Fix the ordinary groupoid $\mathcal I$ with objects $0,1$ and exactly one morphism between each ordered pair, and put $E=N\mathcal I$. Regard $\mathcal I$ and the one-object terminal category as discrete simplicial categories. They are locally Kan, hence Bergner fibrant by [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]: all mapping sets are points, and the equivalence-lifting condition for a terminal map is filled by the identity. The functor $\mathcal I\to *$ is a DK equivalence, since all its mapping maps are identities of points and $\pi_0\mathcal I\to *$ is fully faithful and essentially surjective. For the coherent-nerve Quillen adjunction, [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] says its right adjoint preserves weak equivalences between fibrant objects. Thus $E\to\Delta^0$ is a Joyal weak equivalence, since the coherent nerve on discrete simplicial categories is the ordinary nerve. For every $X$, the endpoints $X\amalg X\hookrightarrow X\times E$ form a monomorphism and the projection $X\times E\to X$ is a categorical equivalence by Step 2. Consequently $X\times E$ is a cylinder with a cofibration as its endpoint inclusion. This construction also works for $X=\varnothing$.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.5.7, printed p.93: replace the chosen two-vertex contractible Kan interval by the nerve of the two-object indiscrete groupoid; Theorem 2.2.5.1 for the nerve adjunction.

proof.text: For every simplicial set $X$ and quasicategory $Q$, [lem-coef-model-localization-homotopy-classes] applies: $X$ is cofibrant because $\varnothing\to X$ is a monomorphism, and $Q$ is fibrant by [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. It says that every element of $[X,Q]_{\mathrm J}$ has an actual simplicial representative and that equality is left homotopy using some cylinder. Equality can in fact be computed with the fixed cylinder $X\times E$ of Step 3. To prove the nontrivial direction, let $J\xrightarrow{c}X$, with endpoints $e_0,e_1$ and $ce_i=1_X$, and $H:J\to Q$ witness equality. Factor $c$ as a trivial cofibration $j:J\to J'$ followed by a fibration $p:J'\to X$; two-out-of-three makes $p$ a trivial fibration. Fibrancy of $Q$ extends $H$ along $j$ to $H':J'\to Q$. Lift the square whose top map is $X\amalg X\xrightarrow{(je_0,je_1)}J'$, bottom map is the projection $X\times E\to X$, left map is the endpoint cofibration, and right map is $p$. The current Joyal model statement supplies both lifting properties through its two mutually characterized weak factorization systems: the trivial cofibration lifts against the terminal fibration of $Q$, and the endpoint cofibration lifts against the trivial fibration $p$. Its filler $a:X\times E\to J'$ makes $H'a$ a homotopy on the fixed cylinder with the prescribed endpoints. Conversely any such fixed-cylinder homotopy is a cylinder homotopy, so the cited equality criterion applies. Hence $[X,Q]_{\mathrm J}$ is precisely the set of actual maps $X\to Q$ modulo homotopies $X\times E\to Q$.

source.place: Proposition 2.2.5.7, printed p.93; fixed-cylinder comparison proved explicitly from the model factorization and lifting axioms.

proof.text:
Choose Joyal fibrant replacements $K\to K^f$ and $L\to L^f$ using [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Their product is a categorical equivalence by Step 2, and $K^f\times L^f$ is fibrant because inner horns can be filled in each coordinate. For any $X$, actual maps $X\to K^f\times L^f$ are pairs of actual maps to $K^f,L^f$. By Step 4, equality of each component in the localization is witnessed on the same fixed cylinder $X\times E$. Pair the two homotopies to get a homotopy into $K^f\times L^f$; conversely any product homotopy projects to the two component homotopies. Surjectivity on representatives and this equality criterion give a bijection
$$[X,K^f\times L^f]_{\mathrm J}\cong[X,K^f]_{\mathrm J}\times[X,L^f]_{\mathrm J}$$
induced by the actual projections. Invert the replacement weak equivalences and the product replacement; their squares with the projections commute, so the same bijection holds for $K,L,K\times L$. It holds for every $X$, which is the product universal property in the ordinary localization. All comparisons are natural because the maps that induce them are the product projections.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 1.2.7.3, printed p.94: product assertion, expanded by fixed-cylinder representatives instead of an uncited general homotopy-product theorem.

proof.text: Strict simplicial currying gives a bijection between actual maps $X\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)$ and maps $X\times K\to Q$. In one direction, evaluate $f_n(x):K\times\Delta^n\to Q$ on $(k,1_{[n]})$; in the other, send $x\in X_n$ to the simplicial map whose value on $(k,\alpha:[m]\to[n])$ is $g_m(X(\alpha)(x),k)$. These constructions are inverse by the simplicial identities, and the forward map is exactly composition with the actual evaluation map.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 1.2.7.3, printed p.94, using Proposition 2.2.5.7; the evaluation and homotopy compatibility are written explicitly.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-joyal-strict-currying] with $X$ replaced by $X\times E$: maps $H:X\times E\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)$ correspond to maps $(X\times E)\times K\to Q$, and composing with the permutation isomorphism $(X\times K)\times E\to(X\times E)\times K$, $(x,k,e)\mapsto(x,e,k)$, to maps $\widetilde H:(X\times K)\times E\to Q$. Naturality of that bijection in its first variable, applied to $1_X\times e_i:X\cong X\times\Delta^0\to X\times E$ for $i=0,1$, says that the transpose of $H\circ(1_X\times e_i)$ is $\widetilde H\circ(1_{X\times K}\times e_i)$, since the permutation carries $(1_{X\times K}\times e_i)$ to $(1_X\times e_i)\times1_K$ under the identifications with products by $\Delta^0$. Hence, for prescribed $f_0,f_1:X\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)$, fixed-cylinder homotopies $X\times E\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)$ from $f_0$ to $f_1$ correspond bijectively to fixed-cylinder homotopies $(X\times K)\times E\to Q$ from $\widetilde f_0$ to $\widetilde f_1$. No fibrancy of $E$ or $Q$ is used.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 1.2.7.3, printed p.94, using Proposition 2.2.5.7; the evaluation and homotopy compatibility are written explicitly.

proof.text:
Step 1 makes $\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)$ fibrant. Apply the representative/equality criterion of Step 4 to $(X,\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q))$ and $(X\times K,Q)$. Step 6 bijects their actual representatives, and Step 7 bijects their fixed-cylinder homotopies with the prescribed endpoints. Passing to these equivalence classes gives
$$[X,\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)]_{\mathrm J}\cong[X\times K,Q]_{\mathrm J}.$$
Its forward map is induced by actual evaluation, and strict naturality follows from Step 6.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 1.2.7.3, printed p.94, using Proposition 2.2.5.7; the evaluation and homotopy compatibility are written explicitly.

proof.text: If $u:Q\to Q'$ is a categorical equivalence between quasicategories, the bijection identifies $[\operatorname{Fun}(K,u)]$ with postcomposition by the isomorphism $[u]$; if $v:K\to K'$ is a categorical equivalence, it identifies $[\operatorname{Fun}(v,Q)]$ with precomposition by the isomorphism $[1_X\times v]$, using Step 2. The categorical Yoneda criterion [lem-coef-joyal-homset-iso-detection] then makes both function-object maps isomorphisms, since their maps on Hom sets are bijective for every $X$. Therefore the strict product and evaluation maps descend through the localization, and the displayed bijections prove the exponential universal property with its specified evaluation and full naturality.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 1.2.7.3, printed p.94, using Proposition 2.2.5.7; the evaluation and homotopy compatibility are written explicitly.

proof.text: For the rigidification assertion, first establish the needed product fact for weak homotopy equivalences without assuming it. Let $f:A\to B$ and $g:C\to D$ be weak homotopy equivalences. By [lem-coef-ex-infinity-finite-products], the units into $\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}$ are weak homotopy equivalences, so naturality and two-out-of-three make $\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}f$ and $\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}g$ weak homotopy equivalences between Kan complexes. The projection $B'\times C'\to B'$ is a Kan fibration whenever $C'$ is Kan: in a horn-lifting square the $B'$ coordinate is prescribed and the $C'$ coordinate is filled by its Kan condition. By right properness in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], the pullback of $A'\to B'$ along this projection is a weak homotopy equivalence $A'\times C'\to B'\times C'$. The same argument with factors interchanged gives $B'\times C'\to B'\times D'$, so their composite is a weak homotopy equivalence. Apply this with primes denoting $\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}$. Its natural product isomorphisms identify that composite with $\operatorname{Ex}^{\infty}(f\times g)$; the unit naturality square and two-out-of-three then show that $f\times g$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. This uses right properness only for the Kan--Quillen structure, not for the Joyal structure.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.5.6, printed p.93: mapping-set product stability used in the proof; expanded using the existing product-preserving Kan replacement and right-properness nodes.

proof.text: It follows that products of two DK equivalences of simplicial categories are DK equivalences. Their maps on mapping simplicial sets are products of weak homotopy equivalences, covered by Step 10. Also $\pi_0(A\times B)\cong\pi_0A\times\pi_0B$: components of a product mapping simplicial set are pairs of components, since edge zigzags project to each coordinate and coordinate zigzags can be combined after inserting identity steps in the other coordinate. Composition and identities act coordinatewise. Hence the induced $\pi_0$ functor is the product of two equivalences: the inverse functors and their natural isomorphisms can be paired. This verifies both parts of the DK definition in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], including for empty object sets.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.5.6, printed p.93: stability of simplicial-category equivalences under products, with the mapping-set and essential-image checks made explicit.

proof.text: For every locally Kan simplicial category $T$, [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] makes $T$ Bergner fibrant and $N_{\mathrm{hc}}T$ Joyal cofibrant. Its Quillen equivalence has an equivalence as its left derived functor. Apply [lem-coef-quillen-derived-counit-criterion] with $L=\mathfrak C$, $U=N_{\mathrm{hc}}$, $Y=T$, and the identity cofibrant replacement of $N_{\mathrm{hc}}T$. It gives a DK equivalence $\epsilon_T:\mathfrak C[N_{\mathrm{hc}}T]\to T$. Now take any $K$, set $A=\mathfrak C[K]$, and use the object-preserving locally Kan replacement $r:A\to RA$ of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Let $v_K:K\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}(RA)$ be the adjoint of $r$. The adjunction identity is the actual equality $\epsilon_{RA}\circ\mathfrak C[v_K]=r$. Since both $r$ and $\epsilon_{RA}$ are DK equivalences, two-out-of-three makes $\mathfrak C[v_K]$ one as well. The detection theorem [lem-coef-rigidification-equivalence-detection] therefore makes $v_K$ a categorical equivalence. Thus every simplicial set admits a categorical equivalence to the coherent nerve of a locally Kan simplicial category, by a construction independent of the product comparison being proved.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.5.6, printed p.93; Theorem 2.2.5.1, derived counit and adjunction triangle identity. This supplies the nerve replacements used there.

proof.text: Write $P_{K,L}:\mathfrak C[K\times L]\to\mathfrak C[K]\times\mathfrak C[L]$ for the functor whose components are rigidifications of the two projections. First let $K=N_{\mathrm{hc}}T$, $L=N_{\mathrm{hc}}U$, with $T,U$ locally Kan. From the defining nerve formula, $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(T\times U)\cong N_{\mathrm{hc}}T\times N_{\mathrm{hc}}U$: a simplicial functor out of each simplex thickening into a product is exactly a pair of such functors. The product $T\times U$ is locally Kan, by filling each horn in each mapping-set coordinate. Under this nerve identification, the composite $(\epsilon_T\times\epsilon_U)P_{K,L}$ equals $\epsilon_{T\times U}$: postcomposing either map with a product projection gives the same map by naturality of the adjunction counit. Step 12 makes all three counits DK equivalences, and Step 11 makes $\epsilon_T\times\epsilon_U$ a DK equivalence. Two-out-of-three proves that $P_{K,L}$ is a DK equivalence in this case.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.5.6, first case of the proof, printed p.93; equality of the actual composite with the counit is checked by projections.

proof.text:
For arbitrary $K,L$, choose the maps $v_K:K\to K'=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(R\mathfrak C[K])$ and $v_L:L\to L'=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(R\mathfrak C[L])$ constructed in Step 12. Naturality of the product projections gives the commuting square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}\mathfrak C[K\times L]&\xrightarrow{P_{K,L}}&\mathfrak C[K]\times\mathfrak C[L]\\ \downarrow\mathfrak C[v_K\times v_L]&&\downarrow\mathfrak C[v_K]\times\mathfrak C[v_L]\\ \mathfrak C[K'\times L']&\xrightarrow{P_{K',L'}}&\mathfrak C[K']\times\mathfrak C[L'].\end{array}$$
Step 2 and [lem-coef-rigidification-equivalence-detection] make the left vertical map a DK equivalence. The same detection theorem and Step 11 make the right vertical map a DK equivalence. Step 13 makes the bottom map a DK equivalence. Two-out-of-three in the Bergner structure of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] therefore makes the actual top map $P_{K,L}$ a DK equivalence. This proves the remaining clause without replacing the specified natural map by an unspecified derived isomorphism.

source.place: Corollary 2.2.5.6, general case, printed p.93; natural replacement square and two-out-of-three.
